messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service `smoke-deploy-healthcheck` (eu-west-1) — high rate of healthcheck failures in smoke canary. INC-20260314-42

pagerduty: INC-20260314-42 -> paging primary on-call: jamal

jamal: acked INC-20260314-42. I'm the on-call, looking now. Any context on what rolled earlier?

alex: I pushed a small kernel-selection tweak in the runtime last night (rollout id r-2026-03-13-76). It hit smoke canary this morning.

maya: seeing a spike in 5xx from the canary hosts, tails show OOM-ish failures around kv-cache alloc. Error log excerpt: 
```
E 03:12:18 inference.cpp:421 KVCache::alloc failed: cannot allocate 256MB
E 03:12:18 worker.cpp:88 response aborted, status=502
```

jamal: ok thanks. alex can you confirm if the canary is still pinned to the new kernel path or if fallback exists?

alex: canary got the new kernel, fallback to old kernel is available but not automatic. I can trigger a rollback for the canary.

sophie: product reports increased error rate for a subset of customers using small-sequence endpoints — estimated affected requests ~0.6% of hosted traffic (auto-routed through canary). No PII impacted, but a handful of alpha customers hit errors.

jamal: priority=high. Impact limited but rolling failure could widen. Plan: 1) stop new canary traffic 2) rollback canary to previous kernel 3) monitor health and begin recovery.

alex: executing rollback now. command: 
```
./deployctl rollback --target r-2026-03-13-76 --env eu-west-1 --scope smoke-canary
```

alex: rollback started. kube rollout status shows pods terminating and recreating with previous image.

ops-bot: rollback job queued: job-id=rb-3319, started by alex. ETA ~45s for pod convergence.

maya: removing canary from traffic routing temporarily. `routectl disable-canary --region eu-west-1`

pagerduty: INC-20260314-42 acknowledged by jamal, assigned to alex (eng-runtime). Next escalation in 10m if unack/unstable.

jamal: watching metrics dashboard — latency and 5xx are trending down already. good sign.

alex: pods back up on previous kernel. healthchecks passing on 6/6 canary instances.

maya: routing restored to stable pool, canary traffic remains disabled until further validation.

sophie: pinged affected customers with a brief note: we detected transient errors and are mitigating; follow-up with timeline after incident.

jamal: marking incident as mitigated. will keep thread open for any regressions. tagging postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260314-42 status -> mitigated. Duration: ~8 minutes.

alex: preliminary root cause: kernel-selection tweak increased memory footprint for short sequences under certain batch shapes, exposed KV cache allocation pressure on small GPU instances. Work items: revert kernel-selection tweak default, add perf test for small-seq memory, add automated canary rollback on healthcheck flaps.

maya: creating ticket: INF-4902 "kernel-selection memory regression — small-seq perf" and linking this thread.

jamal: handing off to next on-call (maya) at 02:00 UTC. i'll add runbook notes in the incident doc.

maya: ack handoff. will monitor next hour, then transition to Eng-Oncall for RCA.

ops-bot: follow-ups created: INF-4902 (assigned alex), INF-4903 (observability thresholds, assigned maya).

sophie: thanks all. Customers updated, support queue notified.

jamal: closing loop: no rollback to stable cluster required. keeping a watch window. I'll add timeline and severity to the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
